1#א: (Siman 101) A piece worthy of honor, etc. The opinion of Terumat HaDeshen: if now, when nullified, it is not important, nevertheless before nullification it was important and is not nullified. The Taz in Orach Chayim siman 473 wondered: from where do we know this — perhaps we follow how it will be after nullification, whether to be lenient or stringent? Terumat HaDeshen has proof from Tosafot in Zevachim on "all sacrifices that became mixed," where the Gemara challenges "let it nullify in the majority" — it is a piece worthy of honor. Tosafot answer from dying sin-offerings with small birds; the challenge on a mixed sin-offering does not apply, for in kodashim there is no worthiness of honor. One cannot say kodashim never have worthiness of honor, for the Mishnah in Avodah Zarah teaches stoned ox, etc. Tosafot in Zevachim and Terumat HaDeshen are correct. Proof from Pesachim: five Paschal lambs, one invalid — we cannot stipulate, for breast and thigh belong to the priest; if the invalid were nullified one against two, there would be no prohibition of eating the Paschal offering improperly; therefore breast and thigh are a piece worthy of honor. See Tosafot at the beginning of "How do we roast." Peri Toar: if benefit-forbidden mixes with eating-forbidden, the Sages did not make worthiness of honor prevent nullification for benefit. In Avodah Zarah, basar b'chalav forbids in any amount — how is nullification possible if taste can be detected? It deals with beast basar b'chalav with fowl where taste cannot be distinguished; taste prohibitions for benefit still apply. Rambam holds beast and fowl are two kinds for worthiness of honor only in its kind — see siman 110. Therefore the Gemara's challenge stands; basar b'chalav teaches both benefit and eating. One should be stringent.
1#ב: And even if the prohibition is only d'rabbanan, there is room to investigate whether a d'rabbanan eating prohibition is nullified. Yevamot teaches that a counted item in a d'rabbanan matter is nullified; terumah in our time is d'rabbanan and is nullified. Tosafot and Rosh discuss bundles of clover in kilayim of a vineyard. For us, who hold only "that which is counted" is not nullified, there is doubt which Tosafot reason applies. End of Avodah Zarah challenges using chametz on Pesach to teach nullification of a d'rabbanan important item. Beit Yosef infers from the Rambam that chullin in the azara has worthiness of honor; the Rambam may hold it is d'oraisa, but after analysis this is uncertain. Rambam in Terumot rules a sealed jug of terumah is not nullified even in a thousand — even d'rabbanan important items are not nullified. Rif holds that without benefit, even beriah is nullified. One may be lenient on non-Jewish cheese in loss cases.
2#א: But if, etc. On this basis Torat Chatat challenged Or Zarua regarding cheese mixed with treifah milk; Peri Chadash and Minchat Yaakov explain Or Zarua as dealing with much treifah milk that was worthy of honor. I do not understand their reading of Or Zarua on cheese curdled in forbidden stomach — perhaps taste of meat absorbed in stomach reabsorbed in milk becomes a prohibition on account of itself; Or Zarua may hold curdling in basar b'chalav does not nullify. Nevertheless, non-Jewish cheese is a prohibition on account of itself because the Sages decreed it — we do not say taste follows the majority for absorbed blood in meat. Rashba's question on fish brine remains; the Sages forbade the brine path, not only the brine. Taz on curdling in neveilah skin is puzzling — sixty is required in milk as explained in siman 87.
2#ב: But the peel, etc. Shach wondered why the Rama derived this from Tosafot in Chullin — only chein nafsho in half a piece is found, not worthiness of honor on a peel. Rabeinu Yerucham holds a peel can be a piece worthy of honor; if squeezing is possible it remains forbidden forever — unlike Tosafot who link piece becoming nevelah with squeezing. We hold like Rabbeinu Tam that a peel does not forbid wet mixtures without sixty; therefore worthiness of honor on a peel in dry mixtures has no place. Ramban ruled well.
3#_: Except chicken in its feathers, etc. Shach challenged the Rama implying a counted item applies; Minchat Yaakov explained the Rama did not mean that. A sheep in its skin is obviously like chicken in feathers — see Peri Chadash and Semak. The Gemara's challenge in "all sacrifices became mixed" — R' Papa answers like the litra of pressed figs — does not resolve for sheep in skin or birds in feathers. Rabbeinu Tam permitted mixed chickens because they are not a counted item when sold in feathers. In our time fowl are not sold in baskets — feathers and skin do not count — see Semak.
6#_: Not in its kind. Derishah uPerishah challenged Or Zarua that worthiness of honor applies only in its kind, citing beriah. The Mishnah in Avodah Zarah is the source; Acharonim in siman 110 wrote "in its kind" is not precise. Rambam in Orlah commentary: everything listed is in its kind with any amount; not in its kind requires sixty. He rules nevelah is nullified in slaughtered animal for tumah — important items are not nullified even for tumah; in not its kind, importance does not help. Cut fish may still be one kind called "piece of fish" unless very thin — see Or Zarua and Peri Chadash on siman 98.
9#_: Head of sheep, etc. Peri Toar wants to be stringent: if we rely on resemblance for a basket of fish when impurity was not established, how can we rely here when impurity was established? One can answer: here all pieces are before us and one matches. Nevertheless signs are rabbinic; we rely on a simple sign plus rabbinic worthiness of honor. Where there is a majority kosher, Torah nullification applies; worthiness of honor is rabbinic. Correct.
